CausalChain: Chronic inflammation in HCC leads to increased IL‐6 secretion → Activation of the JAK2/STAT3 pathway elevates PD‐L1 expression and promotes tumor proliferation → Icaritin intervenes by selectively modulating ERa36 and inhibiting the IL‐6/JAK2/STAT3 cascade, reducing PD‐L1 levels and dampening tumor growth → Residual checkpoint activity still hinders optimal T cell function → Combining icaritin with PD‐1/PD‐L1 immune checkpoint inhibitors could synergistically relieve T cell suppression and overcome tumor resistance
Hypothesis: Co‐administration of icaritin with PD‐1/PD‐L1 inhibitors will synergistically enhance anti-tumor immunity in HCC by modulating the IL‐6/JAK2/STAT3 cascade and downregulating PD‐L1, thereby overcoming the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and improving therapeutic outcomes.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a challenge for treatment due its high heterogeneity, immunosuppressive microenvironment, and complex signaling networks that sustain tumor growth. Recent advances in targeted agents and immunotherapies have offered new avenues for treatment; however, durable responses remain suboptimal. Emerging studies indicate that modulation of cytokine‐driven signaling pathways, particularly the interleukin‐6 (IL‐6)/JAK2/STAT3 axis, may not only drive tumor progression but also contribute to elevated PD‐L1 expression in HCC. Icaritin, a prenylflavonoid implicated in HCC therapy by modulating estrogen receptor (ERa36) and inhibiting the IL‐6/JAK2/STAT3 cascade, has shown potential to reduce PD‐L1 expression and tumor growth. We propose that targeting this pathway with icaritin, thereby “re‐programming” the tumor microenvironment, followed by or combined with PD‐1/PD‐L1 blockade, could synergistically enhance T‐cell mediated antitumor responses. This novel combination strategy may overcome resistance and improve clinical outcomes in HCC patients.
